chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Nu'aym al-Sahhaf, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you love your brethren, O Husayn?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you benefit their poor ones?' I said, 'Yes'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'But, it is an entitlement upon you that you love the one whom Allah loves. But, by Allah, you will not benefit anyone from them until you love him.' I said, 'Yes'.
'Are you inviting them to your house?' I said, 'Yes. I do not eat unless there are two of them with me, and three, and less, and more'.

So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'But their merit upon you is greater than your merit upon them'. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I feed them my food, and I give them my ride, and their merit upon me happens to be greater?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. When they come over to your house, they enter with the Forgiveness for you, and Forgiveness for your dependants, and when they go out from your house, they go out with your sins (having been Forgiven) and the sins of your dependants'.

key_terms.يَحِقُّ عَلَيْكَ: it is an entitlement upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of hosting and feeding the poor among believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates social hospitality to a spiritual mechanism of expiation, teaching that the poor brethren carry the host's forgiveness into their homes and remove their sins upon departure. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *mu'akhat* (brotherhood) as a tangible means of purifying the self, where material generosity is secondary to the spiritual weight of the guest's presence. The narration underscores the reciprocal nature of divine love, linking the believer's affection for the poor directly to Allah's pleasure.

en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Husayn ibn Nu’aim al-Sahhaf who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) asked, ‘Do you love your brothers (in belief) O Husayn?’ I said, ‘Yes, 1 love them.’ The Imam asked, ‘Do you provide any benefit for their poor?’ I said, ‘Yes, I do so.’ The Imam said, ‘It is obligatory for you to love whoever loves Allah. By Allah you will not provide any benefit to any of them unless you love them.
Do you invite them to your house?’ I said, ‘Yes, I do so. I do not eat unless there are two, three men or less or more. ’

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘Their excellence over you is more than your excellence over them.’ I then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I feed them my food on my own table on my furnishings. How can their excellence be greater than my excellence?’

The Imam said, ‘Yes, it is because when they come to your house they bring with them forgiveness for you and for your family and when they leave your house they leave along with your sins and the sins of your family.’”
